reels.format: Reel · face at the start and end, screen in the middle · about 24 s
reels.title: Intro: I'm sending 20 invitations to test a coffee app in Paris
reels.script:
I'm sending 20 invitations to test a coffee app in Paris.
Hey, I'm Franco, a student here in Paris, and I'm building Sumay because I love coffee.
You discover the story behind each café, and cafés hand-picked for you.
It's early: today the cafés are from Quito, and Paris is next.
If you want one of the 20 spots, the link is in my bio.

reels.note:
SHOTS
0:00 to 0:03 Face to camera: the hook. A café table behind you, natural light.
0:03 to 0:20 Your voice over screen recordings of the app: a café page with its story, the page turn in the book, the bean card, the list of Quito cafés.
0:20 to 0:24 Face again: the ask.

BEFORE YOU POST
1. The bio link is live and tested (tag ig).
2. Decide how the 20 are chosen. Suggested: the first 20 Paris signups. Only say 20 if it is true.
3. Pin this comment: “If you sign up, I'll email you if you're one of the first 20.”

The Quito line (“today the cafés are from Quito”) is optional. Delete it if you prefer, but testers will find only Quito cafés and Spanish screens. The line about a future community for coffee lovers was cut for time; add it as on-screen text if you want it. Intro V2 and Intro V3 re-introduce you from other angles later in the stack.

reels.script:
Why not just use Google Maps?
Google Maps and TripAdvisor give you photos and stars. That's about it.
Sumay is local and tailored. It shows you [WHAT the café page shows today: the story, the specialty, the occasion], so you know where you're going and why it's worth it.
And once you've picked the café, Sumay sends you to Google Maps to get there.
If you want to try it, the link is in my bio.

reels.hook: Intro V4: technology can be human
reels.title: Intro: technology can be human
reels.script:
I'm a software engineer, and I believe technology can be human.
If you're tired of AI slop, here's a different idea: technology that connects communities. In this case, coffee.
There's a whole world behind your cup: the process, the origins, the recipes that almost nobody reads because we never have time.
So I'm building a coffee club where every café visit is a small journey: you learn something about the place and the coffee.
[UPDATE: a real result so far, for example how many people joined or how many cafés you were sent].
If you want to follow along, the link is in my bio.

items.text: Stories: Do you care about the story behind your coffee?
items.note:
Story 1 (poll): Do you go to coffee shops? Yes / Yes, all the time.
Story 2 (poll): Last time you were in a café, did you wonder where the beans came from? Yes / No.
Story 3 (question box): Reply with a café whose story I should tell.

Your own wording for Story 2 also works: “When you go to a coffee shop, are you interested in the story behind it, how it's made?” The version about what people did is harder to answer just to be nice. Write down the real numbers. You can use them in Wednesday's Stories and in a Reel, only if they are good.

items.text: Stories: Monday's results + the WhatsApp round
items.note:
Stories: show Monday's real poll numbers, for example “[N]% of you wondered where your beans come from.” Say what you are building next.

WhatsApp round (not a Story): message your ~20 contacts in Paris with the link ?ref=wa and everyone else with ?ref=wain. Suggested message: “Hey! I'm testing Sumay, a coffee app I'm building. Could you do the 1-minute quiz and send it to one friend in Paris? [link]”

Send the Paris link only to people in Paris. Everyone else gets the wain link. That is what keeps the Paris count honest.

items.text: Stories: Behind the scenes in a café
items.note:
Show yourself in a café, filming or editing. One line about what you are working on next. Then answer every DM and comment from the week.

Replies are signals too. If someone replies with a café, thank them and note it for the “Help me pick” Reel.
